texts.facts: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident. She was taken to Government Hospital, Panchanahalli, and thereafter she was shifted to Mangala Hospital, Hassan where she was treated for grievous injuries. A case was registered in Crime No.5/2019 at Panchanahalli Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC against the rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing No.KA-13-EH-5721. Hence, this petition for compensation. 3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondent No.3 appeared through its Counsel and filed written statement. The respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent and hence, placed exparte. The third respondent has denied the entire petition averments as false. Accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 by its rider wherein the petitioner was a pillion rider and the police after due investigation, have filed chargesheet against the said rider. The petitioner has admitted that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.KA-13-EH-5721 by its rider and hence, the respondent No.3 is not a necessary party to this proceedings. The insured i.e., the 2nd respondent has not informed about the alleged accident or any cause of action against the said policy of insurance to the 3 rd respondent. The second respondent and the jurisdictional police have not complied with the mandatory requirements of M.V.Act as required under Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the M.V.Act. Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner during his arguments, has relied upon a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2015)9 SCC 273 (Khenyel Vs New India Assurance Co., Ltd., and Others).
